  "textEditContent": "#!/usr/bin/env python\n\"\"\"\nList Copilot Studio agents (bots) from Dataverse.\n\nCopilot Studio agents are stored in the 'bot' entity in Dataverse.\n\"\"\"\n\nimport sys\nimport os\nfrom datetime import datetime\n\nsys.path.insert(0, os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), \"..\", \"src\"))\n\nfrom powerplatform.client import DataverseClient\n\n\ndef main():\n    print(\"=\" * 80)\n    print(\"COPILOT STUDIO AGENTS\")\n    print(\"=\" * 80)\n    \n    with DataverseClient() as client:\n        # Query the bot entity - this stores Copilot Studio agents\n        # Key fields: name, botid, statecode, statuscode, createdon, modifiedon\n        try:\n            # First, get the list of bots with key fields\n            bots = client._request(\n                \"GET\",\n                \"bots\",\n                params={\n                    \"$select\": \"name,botid,statecode,statuscode,createdon,modifiedon,schemaname,accesscontrolpolicy,language,publishedon\",\n                    \"$orderby\": \"modifiedon desc\"\n                }\n            )\n            \n            bot_list = bots.get(\"value\", [])\n            \n            if not bot_list:\n                print(\"\\nNo Copilot Studio agents found in this environment.\")\n                print(\"\\nThis could mean:\")\n                print(\"  - No agents have been created yet\")\n                print(\"  - The app registration doesn't have permission to read bots\")\n                print(\"  - The bot entity is not available in this environment\")\n                return\n            \n            print(f\"\\nFound {len(bot_list)} agent(s):\\n\")\n            print(\"-\" * 80)\n            \n            for i, bot in enumerate(bot_list, 1):\n                name = bot.get(\"name\", \"Unnamed\")\n                bot_id = bot.get(\"botid\", \"N/A\")\n                schema_name = bot.get(\"schemaname\", \"N/A\")\n                language = bot.get(\"language\", \"N/A\")\n                \n                # State: 0=Active, 1=Inactive\n                state = bot.get(\"statecode\", 0)\n                state_label = \"Active\" if state == 0 else \"Inactive\"\n                \n                # Status codes can vary\n                status = bot.get(\"statuscode\", 1)\n                \n                created = bot.get(\"createdon\", \"\")[:10] if bot.get(\"createdon\") else \"N/A\"\n                modified = bot.get(\"modifiedon\", \"\")[:10] if bot.get(\"modifiedon\") else \"N/A\"\n                published = bot.get(\"publishedon\", \"\")[:10] if bot.get(\"publishedon\") else \"Never\"\n                \n                # Access control: 0=Anonymous, 1=Authenticated\n                access = bot.get(\"accesscontrolpolicy\", 0)\n                access_label = \"Authenticated\" if access == 1 else \"Anonymous\"\n                \n                print(f\"{i}. {name}\")\n                print(f\"   ID:         {bot_id}\")\n                print(f\"   Schema:     {schema_name}\")\n                print(f\"   Language:   {language}\")\n                print(f\"   Status:     {state_label} (statecode={state}, statuscode={status})\")\n                print(f\"   Access:     {access_label}\")\n                print(f\"   Created:    {created}\")\n                print(f\"   Modified:   {modified}\")\n                print(f\"   Published:  {published}\")\n                print()\n            \n            print(\"-\" * 80)\n            print(f\"\\nTotal: {len(bot_list)} agent(s)\")\n            \n        except Exception as e:\n            error_msg = str(e)\n            print(f\"\\n❌ Error querying bots: {error_msg}\")\n            \n            if \"404\" in error_msg or \"Not Found\" in error_msg:\n                print(\"\\nThe 'bots' entity was not found. This could mean:\")\n                print(\"  - Copilot Studio is not provisioned in this environment\")\n                print(\"  - Try querying 'chatbots' entity instead (older API)\")\n            elif \"403\" in error_msg or \"Forbidden\" in error_msg:\n                print(\"\\nAccess denied. The app registration may need:\")\n                print(\"  - 'System Administrator' or 'Bot Author' security role\")\n                print(\"  - Permission to read the bot entity\")\n            else:\n                print(\"\\nTroubleshooting tips:\")\n                print(\"  - Check your DATAVERSE_* environment variables\")\n                print(\"  - Verify the app registration has proper permissions\")\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    main()\n",

}

## Topics (14 total)

### System Topics (13)
These are the default system topics that come with every Copilot Studio agent:

| Topic | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| **Conversation Start** | Triggers when the agent receives an Activity |
| **Conversational boosting** | Creates generative answers from knowledge sources |
| **End of Conversation** | Triggered by a redirect action |
| **Escalate** | Triggered when user indicates they need escalation |
| **Fallback** | Triggers when the user's utterance doesn't match |
| **Goodbye** | Triggers when the user says goodbye |
| **Greeting** | Triggered when the user greets the agent |
| **Multiple Topics Matched** | Triggers when multiple topics match |
| **On Error** | Triggers when the agent encounters an error |
| **Reset Conversation** | Resets the conversation |
| **Sign in** | Triggers when authentication is needed |
| **Start Over** | Restarts the conversation |
| **Thank you** | Triggers when the user says thank you |

### Custom Topics (1)
| Topic | Type |
|-------|------|
| **VSCODE_Experimentation** | Custom GPT/Agent definition (Type 15) |

The user wants to see the details of the "Conversation Start" topic from the VSCODE_Experimentation agent. I need to query the botcomponents entity to get the full content of that topic.## Conversation Start - Summary

**Purpose:** This system topic triggers when the agent receives an Activity indicating the beginning of a new conversation.

### What It Does

When a user starts a new conversation, the agent:

1. **Sends a greeting message**:
   - **Text:** "Hello, I'm {System.Bot.Name}. How can I help?"
   - **Voice/Speak:** "Hello and thank you for calling {System.Bot.Name}. Please note that some responses are generated by AI and may require verification for accuracy. How may I help you today?"

### Structure
| Property | Value |
|----------|-------|
| **Kind** | AdaptiveDialog |
| **Trigger** | OnConversationStart |
| **Action** | SendActivity (greeting message) |

### Notes
- The `{System.Bot.Name}` variable dynamically inserts the agent's name ("VSCODE_Experimentation")
- The voice response includes an AI disclaimer that text responses don't include
- You can disable this topic if you don't want the agent to initiate the conversation automatically

The user is asking about VS Code profiles - a feature that allows switching between different configurations. This is a general VS Code question, not related to the workspace code.Yes! VS Code has **Profiles** built-in. Here's how to use them:

## VS Code Profiles

### Create a Profile
1. **File** → **Preferences** → **Profiles** → **Create Profile**
2. Or use Command Palette: `Ctrl+Shift+P` → "Profiles: Create Profile"

### What Profiles Include
- Settings
- Extensions
- UI state
- Keybindings
- Snippets
- Tasks

### Switch Between Profiles
- Click the **gear icon** (⚙️) in the bottom-left → **Profiles** → Select profile
- Or `Ctrl+Shift+P` → "Profiles: Switch Profile"

### For Different Logins/Environments

For your use case with different logins, you could create profiles like:
- **Work-D365** - with your Dynamics 365 tenant login
- **Personal** - with personal Azure account
- **Client-X** - for specific client environments

Each profile can have:
- Different **Azure Account** extension settings
- Different **GitHub** accounts signed in
- Different environment variables in settings
- Different extensions enabled/disabled

### Quick Profile Indicator
The current profile name appears in the title bar and bottom-left gear icon.

_**Agent (model copilot/claude-opus-4.5)**_

The user is asking about how to set "UI State - start fresh" when creating a VS Code profile. They're in the profile creation dialog.In the profile creation dialog:

1. When you see the **"Copy from"** section, there are checkboxes for what to include:
   - Settings
   - Keyboard Shortcuts
   - User Snippets
   - User Tasks
   - Extensions
   - **UI State**

2. Simply **uncheck "UI State"** to start fresh

If you chose to copy from an existing profile or "Default", just make sure the **UI State** checkbox is **unchecked** (not ticked).

**What UI State includes:**
- Open editors/tabs
- Sidebar state (expanded/collapsed)
- Panel positions
- Recently opened files
- Window layout
- Activity bar state

By unchecking it, your new profile opens with a clean slate - no leftover tabs or layouts from your main profile.

If you've already created the profile and want to reset UI state, you can:
1. `Ctrl+Shift+P` → "Profiles: Show Contents"
2. Find UI State and clear it
